ultrā (+ accusative)

preposition with the accusative; also an adverb

beyond, further than

Past a point, further than it: ultrā līmen, beyond the threshold. As an adverb, further, any more: nec ultrā. Of measure, beyond: ultrā modum.

Other words

  • trāns (+ accusative) — beyond, on the far side of

    preposition with the accusative · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 12.19.1: trāns Tiberim

    Across a river, mountains or the sea (see across).

  • suprā (+ accusative) — beyond (a measure), more than

    preposition with the accusative · also used · classical · Verg. G. 4.236: illīs īra modum suprā est

    Above and beyond a measure (see above).

Examples

  • nam vix eō ultrā līmen ēgressō, trīclīnium illud suprā convīvās corruit

    for he had hardly stepped beyond the threshold when that dining room fell in on the guestsQuint. 11.2.13

  • nūlla jam ultrā gēns, nihil nisi flūctūs et saxa

    there is no people beyond us now, nothing but waves and rocksTac. Agr. 30.5

  • pergeret porrō īre nec ultrā inquīreret

    he should go on further and ask no moreLiv. 21.22.9

  • illīs īra modum suprā est

    their anger is beyond measureVerg. G. 4.236

See also across, over, far.
